text:
maya: Seeing a recurring pattern: HPA spikes based on our external GPU-util metric, but cluster-autoscaler isn't adding nodes quickly enough. Pods end up Pending for ~90-120s because new GPU nodes take time to become Ready (driver install + kubelet).

oliver: Can you paste the HPA + PromAdapter metric config? Might be smoothing/aggregation window mismatch.

maya: Here's the HPA we use (edited for clarity):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: llm-inference-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: llm-worker
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: gpu_util_pct
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 60
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 100
        periodSeconds: 60
```

sasha: stabilizationWindowSeconds=300 means HPA will smooth out spikes for 5m, so it won't aggressively ramp for short bursts. Also PromAdapter might be returning a 1m avg. If CA needs to react faster, HPA smoothing and metric window both matter.

devon: CA shows scale-up events but then backs off:
```
I0312 12:10:14.123] Scale-up: group=gpupool nodes=1 -> 2 (pending: 3)
I0312 12:10:20.456] Node startup: instance gke-gpupool-123 initializing, GPU driver install ongoing
I0312 12:12:00.789] NotReady nodes: 1. Waiting for kubelet cgroups/driver
```

lee: Our GPU images run a post-start init that takes ~45-60s (driver + nvidia-plugin + sidecar init). CA's backoff/grace may be expiring before node is Ready, so it thinks scale-up failed and doesn't try more. Also if pods have strict nodeSelector/gpu-qty, they queue.

maya: So options? Increase HPA aggression? Reduce stabilizationWindow? Tweak PromAdapter metric scraping? Warm pool?

oliver: Quick wins:
- set HPA.behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds to a lower value (e.g., 30) for this deployment only.
- ensure Prometheus adapter returns an instantaneous-ish rate or 30s avg instead of 5m.
- set HPA.target to use AverageUtilization or tune target.

sasha: Longer-term: pre-provision a warm pool of GPU nodes (small, expensive, but keeps cold-start latency down), or use CA cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/expander: priority-order to prefer gpupool when scaling.

devon: Also found CA flags that help: --scale-down-unneeded-time, --max-node-provision-time. We currently have max-node-provision-time=5m which is generous, but scale-up backoff (exponential) can still prevent repeated attempts. Maybe set --max-total-unready-percentage lower? Not sure.

autoscaler-bot: FYI: there was a related incident 2026-01-07 where warm pool fixed >80% of user-facing latency spikes. Link: https://wiki.redwood/infra/warm-pool-case-study :thumbsup:

maya: I prototyped lowering stabilization to 30s and adjusted the metric to 30s avg in PromAdapter. After that we saw faster HPA decisions but still ~40s gap because node init takes time.

lee: Could we change the Deployment to start with a small standby replica that tolerates GPU=0 and migrates when GPU present? Probably messy.

oliver: Another trick: use HPA with an additional custom metric that predicts load (request rate) so HPA reacts before GPU util spikes. Or use predictive scaling: short window polyfit.

maya: For immediate mitigation I'll:
- lower stabilizationWindow to 30 for llm-worker HPA
- adjust PromAdapter scrapes to 30s for gpu_util_pct
- add CA annotation to prioritize gpupool on scale-up:
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-up-priority: "gpupool:1"
```
- open a ticket to evaluate a 2-node warm pool (cost estimate in ticket).

sasha: SGTM. Also add a readinessProbe tweak so pods can tolerate short driver init? e.g., start with --init-sleep that retries more gracefully.

devon: I'll monitor CA logs for failed scale attempts and bump max-node-provision-time if we still see churn.

maya: thanks. I'll post results in ~24h. :rocket:
